summary: The billing crisis that has run this account for five weeks finally moved - and the service side hit its lowest point on record in the same seven days. Lauren closed invoice 3 on Sep 11 with a screenshot and two words: "Invoice completed". That was the fifth payment action on a single invoice, and nobody at ALTR acknowledged it - Stephski's next message, three days later, was a heads-up that another invoice was coming. Then on Sep 15 the thing four consecutive reports have asked for finally happened, partially: invoice 4 went out with "Please note a slight name change to the account, but the same account and wire info. This should help alleviate any bounce backs or issues moving forward." Thirty-four days after ALTR changed the account number and broke the rail, the beneficiary name was corrected. The result was immediate and it is the single best datapoint on this account in a month: Lauren paid invoice 4 in ONE payment, roughly 25 hours after receiving it - "Sent" - after seven $5k Zelle installments and two rejected wires across the previous three weeks. Nobody at ALTR asked whether the wire finally went through, and nobody has ever said one word about the other half of what she reported on Aug 31: "And your account was flagged by Chase for fraud/scam transactions so they won't send it through so they won't send it even if I say so". That is 18 days of silence on a major US bank telling a paying client this agency's account is associated with scam transactions. Stephski also chased invoice 4 twenty-two hours after issuing it - "hi Lauren just making sure you saw this ❤️" - to a client whose payment record across four invoices is spotless. Against that, delivery collapsed. Ollie Mckinlay sent ONE message in seven days: "Hey Lauren - faisal_m1989\n\nSnapchat add please". She added him the same day. That is the entire account-management contribution for the week, and every one of his items aged another seven days untouched - content boundaries 47 days, whale report 42, third custom 34 and still never chased once, CodyBeebs proof 31, livestream 28. Derrek sent nothing for a third straight window and has now been silent for 22 days. And the one service line that had never failed in nine weeks failed: no DMCA/leak-removal report was delivered, breaking a streak unbroken since Jul 17. The bright spots are real and they are both from the wrong people: Mayson and Michelle spent Sep 11-15 actually building something - they untangled the two IG accounts, took over the backup page, stood up the Snapchat funnel, and Lauren delivered her entire side of it (logins, 2FA twice, "Put a ton of photos into the Snapchat drive"). Mayson also announced on Sep 15 "go check your Facebook profile, we have a campaign running!!" - the first sign of paid traffic in 74 days, with no spend figure and no report attached. And Mica Vecco broke a month of silence with an unprompted Instagram security advisory. That advisory closes with "Please do not send your backup codes to anyone, including our team" - six days after ALTR asked for and received her Instagram and Snapchat passwords in plaintext in this group chat, and eleven days after someone was added to it.

health.rationale: Up 2 from 49, and the whole of that increase is billing mechanics. Invoice 3 closed on Sep 11, invoice 4 was issued Sep 15 with the corrected account name that four consecutive reports had demanded, and she paid it in a SINGLE transaction roughly 25 hours later instead of five $5k Zelles - the first frictionless payment since Aug 6. That is a genuine structural improvement and it deserves to move the number. Nothing else improved and several things got worse. The Chase fraud flag she reported on Aug 31 has now gone 18 days without a single ALTR person acknowledging it, and nobody asked or confirmed whether the wire rail actually works again, so the fix is unverified by the people who made it. The 5% paid-ads fee rode a FOURTH invoice with no Meta report in 46 days. Stephski chased the invoice 22 hours after sending it and never acknowledged the payment that closed the previous one. Ollie Mckinlay sent exactly one message in seven days and it was a request of her; seven items aged past 27, 28, 31, 34, 42 and 47 days with zero movement for a fifth straight week. Derrek sent nothing for a third consecutive window - 22 days silent. And the weekly leak-removal report, the only service line on this account that had never needed a reminder in nine weeks, did not arrive. Two new exposures opened this window: her Instagram and Snapchat passwords plus two 2FA codes were posted in plaintext in a group chat that saw a member removed and re-added on Sep 17, and the same password is reused across both accounts. The client is still leaning in hard - 23 messages, every ask closed same-day, her entire Snapchat obligation delivered. That goodwill is now the only thing holding this account up, and it survived this week because the money finally moved cleanly. It will not survive a fifth invoice with no ad report and another week of one message from her account manager.
health.split: Billing/finance: improving. Account management: worst week on record. Client conduct: excellent, unchanged.
